extracted.intended_audience: school administrators, Title IX coordinators, higher-education legal counsel, commenters and stakeholders participating in Title IX rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble section of a federal Title IX rule responding to public comments and explaining regulatory choices, definitions, procedures, and changes made from the NPRM to the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate and credible source citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether sources cited in the NPRM (e.g., blogs, books, media reports) are appropriate, evidence-based, and reflective of a balanced set of perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters criticized use of blogs and certain books (e.g., Laura Kipnis's Unwanted Advances) as suggesting undue engagement with materials promoting gender stereotypes; Department response: NPRM citations demonstrate a range of perspectives (supportive and critical) and warranted consideration, and the Department considered views, perspectives, experiences, opinions, analyses, and data expressed in public comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of intersectionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the regulations and Department actions pay attention to how sex/gender interacts with race and other identities and the potential differential impacts on marginalized populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters urged an intersectional approach; Department emphasizes final regulations apply to all individuals irrespective of race or other demographic characteristics and provides protections intended to supportively, fairly, and accurately address allegations for the benefit of every individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived agency bias and motive
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns that Department statements or cited officials' remarks indicate gender bias in the rulemaking process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters cited media reports of statements by public officials as evidence of bias; Department states no reported statement suggests bias against women and reiterates commitment to principles balancing survivors' rights and respondents' due process (referencing Secretary DeVos's stated 'non-negotiable principles').

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on reporting rates and campus safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the proposed regulations will discourage reporting, chill victims from reporting, increase underreporting, or make campuses less safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued rules would chill reporting and embolden predators; Department disagrees, reasoning that predictable, consistent rules increase likelihood of prompt, supportive, fair responses and noting regulatory changes to encourage reporting (expansion of 'actual knowledge', required contact info display, ability to report anytime, and requirement to offer supportive measures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'actual knowledge'
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes 'actual knowledge' for a recipient to have an obligation to respond under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department expanded §106.30 to include reports to any elementary or secondary school employee and to expressly include a report to the Title IX Coordinator, clarifying when recipient obligations trigger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and visibility of Title IX Coordinator contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that recipients prominently display Title IX Coordinator contact information and allow reporting via that contact information at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised §106.8 requires recipients to prominently display Title IX Coordinator contact info on websites, state that any person may report using that info, and that reports may be made at any time (including non-business hours) via phone, email, or mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to supportive measures regardless of formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation to offer supportive measures to complainants whether or not a formal complaint is filed or a grievance process is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(a) revised to require recipients to offer supportive measures to every complainant; Title IX Coordinator must promptly contact complainant, discuss supportive measures, consider complainant's wishes, and explain the option of filing a formal complaint. Supportive measures are designed to help preserve equal access to education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'complainant'
rubrics_metrics.description: Who qualifies as a 'complainant' under the regulations and thus who is entitled to supportive measures and protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.30 definition of 'complainant' revised to mean any individual 'who is alleged to be the victim' of sexual harassment, clarifying that offer of supportive measures applies even if the complainant is not the person who made the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial grievance process and truth-seeking
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must be impartial, truth-seeking, and treat all parties without bias, prejudice, or stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations prescribe a grievance process designed to impartially evaluate all relevant evidence so determinations are accurate and reliable; treating parties with dignity, respect, and sensitivity fosters impartiality and truth-seeking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearing cross-examination protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Protections governing live hearings and cross-examination to avoid traumatizing complainants and to ensure impartial procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination in live hearings at postsecondary institutions must never involve parties personally questioning each other; at a party's request, hearings can occur with parties in separate rooms using technology enabling participants to see and hear each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma-informed considerations and accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of trauma's neurobiological effects and ensuring procedures account for traumatized complainants without prejudging facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department recognizes developing science on trauma; final regulations contain provisions (e.g., supportive measures, separate rooms for hearings, restricted cross-examination) intended to take into account that complainants may be suffering results of trauma while preserving impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of sexual assault within Title IX sexual harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether sexual assault (including rape), domestic violence, dating violence, and stalking are covered as Title IX sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department included sexual assault in the definition of Title IX sexual harassment to ensure clarity that even a single instance of rape is covered under Title IX; coverage requires actual knowledge that the incident occurred in the recipient's education program or activity in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and limits (including supportive measures confidentiality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations to keep identities confidential and when confidentiality may be breached (e.g., FERPA, as required by law, or necessary to conduct Title IX proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.71(a) requires recipients to keep confidential identities of individuals who made reports/complaints, complainants, respondents, and witnesses unless permitted by FERPA, required by law, or necessary to conduct proceedings; §106.30 instructs recipients to keep supportive measures confidential except as necessary to provide them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on retaliation and First Amendment protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits retaliation against individuals exercising Title IX rights and clarifies that exercise of First Amendment rights is not retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added §106.71 prohibits retaliation intended to interfere with Title IX rights and §106.71(b) states that the exercise of rights protected by the First Amendment is not retaliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation to Title IX sexual harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations apply only to Title IX sexual harassment and do not create new obligations for non-Title IX harassment or other topics outside the NPRM scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department declines to address topics outside original NPRM scope (e.g., pregnancy/parenting, fraternities/sororities, athletics, forms of harassment other than sexual). Response obligations in §106.44 and grievance process in §106.45 apply only to Title IX sexual harassment; other civil rights laws and disability law regulations remain applicable for non-Title IX allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion over internal affairs and discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules are designed to obligate recipients to respond supportively and resolve allegations fairly without encroaching on recipients' discretion over internal academic, administrative, and disciplinary decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department declines to require or prescribe disciplinary sanctions (discipline decisions remain within recipients' discretion) and declines requirements that would restrict First Amendment rights; many commenter-suggested practices that concern internal affairs may be adopted by recipients while complying with regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement authority and limits on altering private rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Department's enforcement role, ability to impose sanctions, and inability to alter judicially-implied private rights of action or remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department will vigorously enforce final regulations under existing statutory/regulatory frameworks (including potential termination of federal financial assistance), but cannot affect the existence of private rights of action under Title IX or change remedies available through private lawsuits; changes to OCR's Case Processing Manual are outside scope of this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity measures to encourage reporting (reporting mechanics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory changes intended to make reporting clearer and easier for complainants to access school responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include requiring prominent posting of Title IX Coordinator contact info, allowing anyone to report using that info, permitting reporting at any time (phone/email/mail), and obligating recipients to promptly offer supportive measures upon a report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling allegations involving multiple bases of harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: How allegations that involve sexual harassment plus harassment on other protected bases should be handled under the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department clarifies that §106.44 and §106.45 response obligations apply only to Title IX sexual harassment; allegations involving other bases may be referred to recipient's Title IX Coordinator and other civil rights regulations (e.g., Title VI, IDEA, Section 504, ADA) continue to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for additional measures (prevention, monitoring, reporting, resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public suggestions for broader measures (e.g., zero-tolerance policies, cameras, third-party monitoring, funding increases, school rating systems) and whether the Department will implement them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department appreciated suggestions but generally declines to require such measures in the final regulations, noting many are within recipients' discretion to adopt and some would require Department action outside the rulemaking's focus; Department added §106.71 on retaliation/confidentiality but declined to adopt other suggested practices as regulatory mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culturally-sensitive services and staff hiring guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests that institutions commit to culturally-sensitive services for students of color and follow hiring guidelines for Title IX offices to ensure fair judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters proposed guidelines for hiring Title IX staff and culturally-sensitive services; Department acknowledged the request but did not adopt such specific requirements into the final regulations, noting recipients may choose to implement them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and national reporting concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the final regulations will affect national data on sexual assault prevalence/reporting and thus impact funding/support services that rely on accurate data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters worried the rules would weaken reporting and skew data; Department stated it does not believe the final regulations will impact the accuracy of national data collection efforts.
